date_note: The page gives only its publication day (25 November); the date of the intrusion is not stated.
title: Deichmann says attackers accessed customer data in its German online store, per Der Spiegel
summary: Hackers accessed personal data of customers of Deichmann's online store in Germany, according to Der Spiegel as relayed by UA.NEWS. Deichmann said names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers and the payment method chosen at checkout may have been affected, and that login details, passwords and payment data were not stolen. It says it stopped the access, closed the vulnerability and has no indications the data was misused.
plain: Deichmann says attackers accessed some customer data in its German online store. It says names, contact details and the chosen payment method may be affected, but not passwords or payment data.
exec: Deichmann reports unauthorised access to customer data in its German online store; it says the access was stopped and it has no indications of misuse.
action: As Deichmann advises, be alert to phishing; the company says it never asks for passwords or payment data by email, phone or SMS.

validation.note: Only UA.NEWS, relaying Der Spiegel and Deichmann's statement, was read; the Spiegel article and Deichmann's own notice were not found.
